purpose: Let Cris configure first-available, uniform random per big task, or Jev task-fit builder selection while keeping one family through steps/fixes/resumes. Usage limits and new visual design preference are optional; model strengths and cautions remain available.
mechanism: lib/roles.js validates optional roles.builder.pick {mode,design?,reservePercent?}, preserves legacy role output, filters paused/excluded members, conservatively reads cached usage, applies explicit design preference, and returns one family/id/effort packet. bin/model-id.mjs exposes --pick builder --json with --design, repeatable --exclude and bounded --task-file; only Jev mode when needed invokes one fixed bounded CLI subprocess with JSON stdin, validated confidence and deterministic fallback. lib/roles-panel.js exposes policy and refuses new fields against stale installed readers before writes. lib/describe.js preserves omitted existing policy in preview and acceptance. lib/models-panel.js retains design-family references for removal checks. public/app.js and styles add four controls and explain task ownership/design limits in the existing editor. guideText emits policy guidance only when configured. Both build SKILLs record packet/operator-named/exclusions in existing plan/handoff, reuse it through phases/fixes/resumes, dispatch native same-vendor workers or supported cross-vendor CLI including native agy, and pass the actual author to review. Explicit operator names preserve existing direct-family semantics. README and docs/neon-builder.md explain use and integration; agy wall/default read-only code is unchanged, served model remains unverified. The fixed cross-vendor Claude dispatcher receives only the phase brief's validation/staging/commit Bash rules through --allowedTools, stays in acceptEdits with empty strict MCP, and safely omits empty optional arrays under Mac Bash3 nounset. Saved records must have a configured builder family and the current matching registry id; automatic paused-owner dispatch is stopped, historical attribution and explicit named paused overrides stay distinct. A real headless Claude fixture edit/test/commit passed with the fixed assertion unchanged and no permission denials.
decisions: Keep existing ordered defaults and deterministic --role output; optional policy only. No shared rotation cursor, scheduler or workflow database. Uniform random has no model-profile weight; new visual direction is explicitly marked by the orchestrator, other work uses ordinary selection. Missing/stale/ambiguous quota evidence leaves a candidate eligible with a reason; all authoritatively excluded returns unavailable. Absent reserve disables filtering, zero skips exhaustion. Jev only selects in its own mode and fails to first eligible. No live quota refresh or provider/model build calls are needed by selection tests. Source worktree is one goal/one PR; full-suite placement is Mini except four established laptop prerequisites. Interactive computer use stopped at Cris's interview; browser acceptance uses private headless Mini Chrome. The optional task-summary reader hardening is filed LOW6/100: a steered caller already has a shell. The caller-written bounded summary is passed to the external Jev CLI when Jev mode needs a decision; do not claim secret-identity or symlink refusal. Internal QA target details are redacted in the public projection; do not reintroduce them.
readers: README and usage docs are for operators configuring builders. SKILL.md twins are executable instructions for orchestrators and are untouchable: report proposals only. Comments are for future maintainers and explain constraints/traps, not the code steps. Build reports are immutable evidence, not editorial docs.
